title: Canary Safety Mesh: phased rollforward with dependency validation and rollback scoring
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
Redwood's progressive delivery tooling currently supports percent ramps, basic canaries and manual rollbacks, but we lack a lightweight, dependency-aware gating layer that prevents noisy rollouts when dependent services (storage, KV cache, compilation) are degraded. This ticket prototypes and implements a 'Canary Safety Mesh' — a set of runtime checks and scoring heuristics that run during a staged rollforward and can automatically pause or rollback traffic when cross-service dependency signals or application-level regressions exceed safe thresholds.

Goals:
- Prevent broad rollouts when dependent infra (e.g., KV cache nodes, model compiler pool) shows elevated error or latency rates.
- Integrate with feature flags so experiments can be mined but fail safely without user-visible errors.
- Implement a penalty-based rollback scorer that aggregates signal deltas (latency p95, error rate, token cost spikes, e2e errors) and triggers automated rollback if score > threshold.
- Preserve fast canaries for low-risk changes (config, small optimizations) while enforcing stricter gates for runtime/hardware or model-variant changes and LTS channel promotions.
- Provide clear telemetry + runbook entries for SREs and release engineers.

Approach / Design:
1) Dependency Validation Layer: at rollout start we borrow the existing health API and augment it with 'dependency probes' that check: KV cache hit rate, compiler queue latency, GPU health (SM utilization spikes), region-specific network latency. Each probe returns a normalized health score (0..100). Rollout will refuse to exceed 5% traffic if any dependency score < 70 unless an explicit override is recorded.

2) Canary Safety Mesh Agents: extend the rollout controller to create short-lived 'mesh agents' that subscribe to telemetry streams (trace sampling, error event counts, infra metrics) for the cohort under test. Agents compute windowed deltas vs baseline and emit a composite 'risk score'.

3) Rollback Scoring: risk score = weighted sum of deltas (service error delta, p95 delta, user-facing error delta, downstream 5xx delta, token-cost delta). Default weights tuned conservatively; higher weights for customer-impacting diffs. If score exceeds a configurable threshold (default 0.7), controller automatically steps down traffic and triggers rollback.

4) Feature Flag Integration: the rollout uses flags to gate both traffic and feature permutations. Flags are deployed first in 'silent mode' (sampling only) for 1% of traffic to gather data; when combined with dependency validation and risk score below threshold, the rollout proceeds with the defined percent ramp.

5) LTS Channel Behavior: promotions to an LTS channel get stricter rules: dependency score threshold + risk thresholds reduced by 30%, and an extended canary window (minimum 24h for runtime and model-substantive changes).

6) Observability & Alerts: expose the following dashboards: rollout overview, dependency health per region, risk score timeline, top error buckets triggered during canary. Alerts: Pager duty policy triggers if auto-rollback occurs or if dependency score drops during a ramp.

Implementation Tasks:
- Add dependency probes to rollout controller (controller changes + lightweight probe infra) (ENG backend).
- Implement mesh agent subscription to telemetry (traces/metrics) with windowed delta computation (telemetry team).
- Implement rollback scoring engine + config UI in Console (backend + frontend).
- Wire feature-flag silent-mode and gradual enablements into rollout controller (FF SDK changes).
- Add LTS channel override rules and metadata in release registry.
- Create dashboards and preset alerts in Grafana/Observability.
- Author runbook for SREs with manual override steps and steps to interrogate risk score components.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A rollout can be started that performs dependency validation and aborts at start if a dependency score < configured threshold.
- Risk score computes and displays in Console in near-real-time and is persisted to rollout audit logs.
- Auto-rollback triggers when score > threshold during a percent ramp and rollback is visible in rollout history with reasoning and metric slices.
- Feature flags can be used in silent sampling mode and tied to rollout cohorts.
- LTS promotions require stricter checks and cannot be force-promoted without explicit documented override and an approval event.
- Documentation (Confluence) and runbook created; at least one canary run executed in staging that demonstrates auto-rollback from a synthetic dependency fault.

Design Docs / Links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Canary+Safety+Mesh (design draft)
- Proposal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1628 (controller + probes)
- FF SDK change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ff-sdk/pull/87

Rollout Plan / Timelines:
- Feb 20 - Mar 6: Prototype mesh agent + dependency probes in staging (POC complete).
- Mar 8 - Mar 18: Implement controller integration + scoring engine, Console visibility.
- Mar 19 - Mar 26: Staging runs and chaos injection tests (KV latency spikes, compiler backlog).
- Mar 27: Production enablement for non-LTS routine rollouts behind a kill-switch feature flag.

Safety and Manual Overrides:
- Any auto-rollback records a reason and opens a remediation issue in the 'release-telemetry' board.
- Manual override requires two approvers if rolling beyond 25% traffic.

Notes on trade-offs and decisions made:
- We intentionally keep simple normalized probes rather than full dependency graph analysis in first iteration to minimize runtime cost.
- Risk scoring uses simple weighted aggregation to keep behavior explainable; ML-based anomaly detection considered for future iteration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller refuses to progress if any dependency probe < configured threshold. 2) Risk score is computed for each canary window and visible in Console with at least 10s resolution. 3) Auto-rollback triggers and fully reverses traffic in <= 2 minutes when threshold exceeded. 4) LTS promotion path requires documented override approval and cannot be automated without explicit consent.
tasks:
- Add dependency probe endpoints and normalizers
- Extend rollout controller to call probes at start and between ramps
- Implement mesh agent to compute windowed deltas (10s/60s windows)
- Build scoring engine and expose configuration in Console
- Wire FF SDK silent-mode sampling and cohort tagging
- Add Grafana dashboards + alerting rules
- Write runbook and conduct a staged chaos test in staging
- Postmortem template for any auto-rollback incidents

release_notes_blurb: Introduce Canary Safety Mesh: dependency-aware rollout gating, automated rollback scoring, and silent-mode feature flag sampling for safer progressive deliveries.
notes: Prototype has shown that mesh agent smoothing is necessary to reduce false positives; default thresholds conservative. Future work: anomaly-detection upgrade and dependency graph correlation.
